mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the same month as the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month of decision
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer wealth and corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for two consecutive months starting at decision date
failure_condition: During the two months following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of instances (empirical p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO below 100 (monthly) coincident with a decline in HOUST signals weak manufacturing and consumer demand, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates prolonged contraction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 AND HOUST < previous_month HOUST in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with the composite signal (Spearman's rho < -0.2, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 growth rate (ΔΔGDPC1 > 0) above the prior month's trend predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as strong quarterly demand forecasts boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: Across 10 such acceleration events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for three consecutive months during a period of rising CPIAUCSL (monthly), the S&P 500 is expected to post positive 60-day forward returns as lower policy rates offset inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL > previous_month CPIAUCSL for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the three-month window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during a matched high-rate inflation window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS below 138,000 in a month with UNRATE < 4.0% predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak labor market participation coincides with low wage growth and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 138000 AND UNRATE < 4.0% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market soft landing turning weak
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS falling below 360,000 while HOUST remains flat or rising suggests resilient demand but persistent supply-side constraints, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 360000 AND HOUST >= previous_month HOUST in the same month
failure_condition: During 20 such events, the 5-day forward return is not negative on average (mean <= 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in CPIAUCSL below 205 for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged signals disinflation, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as markets anticipate rate hold or cut.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 205 AND FEDFUNDS == previous_month FEDFUNDS for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 8 such disinflation episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than during comparable inflationary holds (bootstrap p > 0.05).
